key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can infer both the motion state and hydrodynamic coefficients of floating bodies directly from time-series movement data by embedding the Cummins equations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven way to identify added mass, damping, and restoring terms for offshore floating structures when direct force measurements are unavailable.
method: Formulate the Cummins equations as a first-order dynamical system.
Use a PINN to estimate translational and rotational states from motion data.
Solve the inverse problem to recover hydrodynamic coefficients from the learned dynamics.
evidence_signal: The method was validated on free-decay cases for a sphere and a box, showing accurate state and coefficient estimation from motion data.
watch_item: Accuracy depends strongly on the volume and quality of available movement data, so sparse or noisy measurements may limit reliability.
paper_title: Estimating Hydrodynamic Coefficients for Floating Offshore Structures from Movement Data Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
